content.text: /ext:medcp In IBD, which extraintestinal comorbidities are most frequent, and what immune signaling could underlie this?
I'll query the EHR database to find the most frequent extraintestinal comorbidities in IBD patients.

This is an OMOP CDM database. I'll first identify the IBD cohort (Crohn's disease + ulcerative colitis via concept ancestry), then rank co-occurring conditions, filtering to plausible extraintestinal manifestations/comorbidities.

arguments.sql_query:
SELECT c.concept_id, c.concept_name, COUNT(DISTINCT co.person_id) AS n_pts
FROM omop.concept c
JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca ON ca.ancestor_concept_id = c.concept_id
JOIN omop.condition_occurrence co ON co.condition_concept_id = ca.descendant_concept_id
WHERE c.concept_name IN ('Crohn''s disease','Ulcerative colitis','Inflammatory bowel disease')
GROUP BY c.concept_id, c.concept_name
ORDER BY n_pts DESC;

content.text: Good — a clean IBD cohort. Now I'll build the IBD person set and rank co-occurring conditions, then focus on recognized extraintestinal categories (arthropathy, skin, eye, hepatobiliary/PSC, VTE, anemia, osteoporosis).

arguments.sql_query:
WITH ibd AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT co.person_id
  FROM omop.concept_ancestor ca
  JOIN omop.condition_occurrence co ON co.condition_concept_id = ca.descendant_concept_id
  WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id = 4074815
),
tot AS (SELECT COUNT(*) n FROM ibd)
SELECT c.concept_name,
       COUNT(DISTINCT co.person_id) AS n_pts,
       ROUND(100.0*COUNT(DISTINCT co.person_id)/(SELECT n FROM tot),1) AS pct
FROM omop.condition_occurrence co
JOIN ibd ON ibd.person_id = co.person_id
JOIN omop.concept c ON c.concept_id = co.condition_concept_id
WHERE co.condition_concept_id <> 0
GROUP BY c.concept_name
ORDER BY n_pts DESC
LIMIT 60;

The general list is dominated by GI symptoms and common comorbidities. Let me target the recognized extraintestinal manifestation (EIM) categories specifically, so I can rank the ones with true immune-mediated links.

arguments.sql_query:
WITH ibd AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT co.person_id
  FROM omop.concept_ancestor ca
  JOIN omop.condition_occurrence co ON co.condition_concept_id = ca.descendant_concept_id
  WHERE ca.ancestor_concept_id = 4074815
),
tot AS (SELECT COUNT(*) n FROM ibd)
SELECT c.concept_name,
       COUNT(DISTINCT co.person_id) AS n_pts,
       ROUND(100.0*COUNT(DISTINCT co.person_id)/(SELECT n FROM tot),1) AS pct
FROM omop.condition_occurrence co
JOIN ibd ON ibd.person_id = co.person_id
JOIN omop.concept c ON c.concept_id = co.condition_concept_id
WHERE c.concept_name IN (
  'Arthritis','Spondyloarthropathy','Ankylosing spondylitis','Sacroiliitis','Psoriatic arthropathy','Enteropathic arthropathy','Peripheral enthesopathy',
  'Erythema nodosum','Pyoderma gangrenosum','Psoriasis',
  'Uveitis','Episcleritis','Scleritis','Iritis','Anterior uveitis',
  'Primary sclerosing cholangitis','Sclerosing cholangitis','Autoimmune hepatitis',
  'Aphthous ulcer','Aphthous stomatitis',
  'Osteoporosis','Osteopenia',
  'Venous thromboembolism','Deep venous thrombosis','Pulmonary embolism',
  'Iron deficiency anemia','Anemia'
)
GROUP BY c.concept_name
ORDER BY n_pts DESC;

I now have quantified EIM frequencies in this IBD cohort (n=27,774). Here's the answer.

## Most frequent extraintestinal comorbidities in IBD (this cohort, n=27,774)

| Category | Condition | Patients | Prevalence |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Hematologic** | Anemia | 7,514 | 27.1% |
| | Iron-deficiency anemia | 3,472 | 12.5% |
| **Musculoskeletal** | Arthritis (peripheral) | 3,020 | 10.9% |
| | Osteoporosis | 2,171 | 7.8% |
| | Osteopenia | 1,016 | 3.7% |
| | Ankylosing spondylitis | 409 | 1.5% |
| **Metabolic/bone** | Vitamin D deficiency | 4,289 | 15.4% |
| **Skin** | Psoriasis | 921 | 3.3% |
| | Pyoderma gangrenosum | 223 | 0.8% |
| | Erythema nodosum | 202 | 0.7% |
| **Thrombotic** | Pulmonary embolism | 612 | 2.2% |
| | Deep vein thrombosis | 457 | 1.6% |
| **Hepatobiliary** | Primary sclerosing cholangitis | 469 | 1.7% |
| | Autoimmune hepatitis | 123 | 0.4% |
| **Ocular** | Uveitis | 173 | 0.6% |
| | Scleritis / episcleritis / iritis | ~200 combined | ~0.7% |

**Ranking:** the dominant extraintestinal burden is **anemia** (mostly iron-deficiency, ~27%), then **arthropathy/arthritis** (~11%) and **metabolic bone disease** (osteoporosis + vitamin D deficiency, ~15% D-deficiency). The classic "immune-mediated EIMs" (arthritis, PG, erythema nodosum, uveitis, PSC) follow the expected relative ordering — arthropathy is the single most common true EIM, and the skin/eye/hepatobiliary manifestations are individually uncommon (<3.5%). Note anemia and vitamin D deficiency are partly consequences of gut inflammation/malabsorption rather than parallel autoimmune targets, so they inflate the "comorbidity" count.

## Immune signaling that could underlie the shared inflammation

The EIMs cluster because IBD and its extraintestinal targets share **barrier-tissue innate + Th17/Th1 circuitry**, with gut-primed lymphocytes trafficking to joints, skin, eye, and liver:

- **IL-23 / Th17 axis (IL-17A, IL-22, GM-CSF).** The strongest unifying pathway. IL-23R risk alleles are shared across IBD, ankylosing spondylitis, psoriasis, and uveitis. Gut-primed Th17 cells and IL-23–responsive innate cells at "entheseal" and barrier sites drive the arthropathy–skin–eye triad. Clinically this is why anti–IL-23/IL-12-23 (ustekinumab, risankizumab) and, in the SpA/skin space, anti–IL-17 agents work — though anti–IL-17 can paradoxically worsen gut disease, underscoring tissue-specific IL-17 biology.
- **TNF-α.** Central shared effector; anti-TNF response across IBD, peripheral arthritis, PG, erythema nodosum, and uveitis reflects a common TNF-driven granulomatous/neutrophilic program.
- **Gut→tissue lymphocyte trafficking (α4β7 / MAdCAM-1, and CCR9).** Aberrant homing of mucosal effector lymphocytes to synovium, skin, and hepatobiliary endothelium ("gut–joint" and "gut–liver" axes). PSC is thought to arise from gut-primed T cells recruited to liver via aberrant MAdCAM-1/CCL25 expression on hepatic endothelium.
- **Neutrophil-driven innate inflammation (IL-1β, IL-8/CXCL, IL-36).** Underlies the neutrophilic dermatoses pyoderma gangrenosum and erythema nodosum.
- **Th1/IFN-γ and dysregulated Treg/IL-10.** Contributes to granulomatous Crohn's-type inflammation and loss of tolerance at multiple barriers.
- **Systemic inflammatory / IL-6–hepcidin axis.** Drives the anemia of inflammation (hepcidin blocks iron export → functional iron deficiency) layered on true iron/vit-D deficiency and bone loss — connecting the most prevalent "comorbidities" back to the same cytokine milieu.

**Caveats:** these are cohort prevalences from coded EHR data (concept-based counts, no age/sex standardization or control comparison), so they show relative burden within IBD, not causal risk ratios. The mechanistic pathways are well-supported by genetics and trial data but remain associative at the individual-patient level.
